title: test_view_interaction.gd copies gesture helpers byte-identically from test_gesture.gd
evidence:
tests/test_view_interaction.gd:227 `func _press(pos: Vector2) -> void:
	var e := InputEventMouseButton.new()
	e.button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT
	e.pressed = true
	e.position = pos
	e.global_position = pos
	Input.parse_input_event(e)
	await tree.process_frame
	await tree.process_frame` is byte-identical to tests/test_gesture.gd:93; `_move` (:238/:104), `_release` (:248/:114) and `_pair_with_arc` (:208/:131, body `var diff: float = absf(Geodesic.arc_angle(sites[i].global_position, sites[j].global_position) - target)`) are also identical. Both files extend "res://tests/test_base.gd".
detail: Four helper bodies are duplicated across two test scripts sharing the same base class; a fix to one copy (e.g. frame-count) silently misses the other.
recommended_fix: Hoist _press/_move/_release/_pair_with_arc into tests/test_base.gd (they only use tree/Geodesic) and delete the per-file copies.

title: REPLAY_CMDS spine duplicated verbatim in capture_runner._e2_shots despite 'ONE definition' claim
evidence:
tests/test_sim_base.gd:9-11 claims `## The replay-evidence command stream — ONE definition shared by
## tests/test_sim_replay.gd and tools/determinism_log.gd so the committed
## capture and its sibling test can never drift apart.` yet scripts/capture_runner.gd:88-93 hardcodes the same 16 pairs again: `for pair in [
		[1, 0], [2, 0], [3, 0], [4, 0],
		[0, 9], [10, 9], [12, 9], [13, 9],
		[9, 11], [13, 11], [15, 11], [17, 11],
		[11, 22], [23, 22], [25, 22], [27, 22],` — exactly REPLAY_CMDS' add_pipe a/b values.
detail: The three-wedge spine now lives in two places; editing REPLAY_CMDS won't update the committed flow/QoS captures, so capture evidence can drift from the pinned replay scenario.
recommended_fix: Have capture_runner._e2_shots build its pairs from load("res://tests/test_sim_base.gd").REPLAY_CMDS add_pipe entries (as tools/determinism_log.gd already does).

title: Determinism capture applies REPLAY_CMDS at tick 300, replay test at tick 120 — different scenarios
evidence: tools/determinism_log.gd:30 `if t == ticks / 3:` (=300 of REPLAY_TICKS 900) vs tests/test_sim_replay.gd:22 `if t == 120:` — same REPLAY_CMDS, different application tick. The committed captures/05-replay-determinism.txt (hashA 3268ebfb/0e435331/20ffef81...) therefore evidences a different replay than the one the byte-identity test pins.
detail: Shared CMDS but divergent timing means the committed capture's per-tick hashes can't be cross-checked against the test's run; 'aligned CMDS' (spec artifact) overstates the alignment.
recommended_fix: Pick one canonical application tick (e.g. a REPLAY_CMD_TICK const in test_sim_base.gd) used by both test_sim_replay.gd and determinism_log.gd.
